name: Eagle Nebula
tagline: Home of the Pillars of Creation — towers of gas where stars ignite.
history: In 1995 Hubble photographed three finger-like columns of cold gas inside the Eagle Nebula and produced the most famous space image ever made: the Pillars of Creation. Each pillar is a four-light-year tower of hydrogen and dust being eroded by the ultraviolet of a young star cluster, with infant stars hatching at their tips — denser knots sheltering embryonic suns. JWST revisited them in 2022 in infrared, revealing hundreds of newly forming stars hidden inside the columns. Some astronomers calculate a supernova shock may already have destroyed the pillars, with the light of their ruin still centuries from reaching us.
